clue.text: Guarantee securing a boy for a limited period

indicators.note: to secure something is to hold it fast within, so the guarantee wraps round what follows

parts.note: a seal is a mark that guarantees authenticity
a boy is someone's son

explanation.surface: A warranty that covers a lad only for a set term.
explanation.definitionFit: Something seasonal lasts only for a particular season, a limited stretch of the year.

clue.text: Brought up American lad to be sentimental

indicators.note: in a down answer, brought up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: Gary is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A boy raised in America grows soppy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brought up' turns US into SU above GARY.
explanation.definitionFit: Sugary describes something cloyingly sweet in feeling, mawkishly sentimental.

clue.text: Topless Antipodeans going to Thailand make Greek tense

indicators.note: topless means the first letter is removed

parts.note: Maoris are the indigenous people of New Zealand, in the Antipodes
T is the international vehicle code for Thailand

explanation.surface: Bare-chested Australasians heading to Thailand tense up in a Greek way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Topless' takes M off MAORIS to leave AORIS.
explanation.definitionFit: The aorist is the simple past form of verbs in ancient Greek grammar.

clue.text: Dishevelled blouse bears the mark of the printer

indicators.note: dishevelled means messed up, so the letters of blouse are disordered

explanation.surface: A rumpled blouse carries a printer's ink stain.
explanation.definitionFit: An obelus is the dagger sign used in printing to mark a footnote.

clue.text: America's finest take gold — a change for the better

parts.note: Am is an abbreviation for America or American

indicators.note: to take something is to hold it, so the finest go round the gold and a

parts.note: the elite are the best of the best
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: The top US athletes win gold, a welcome improvement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a' is a letter of the wordplay, so the definition is the verb phrase 'change for the better'.
explanation.definitionFit: To ameliorate is to improve something or make it better.

clue.text: Model put on a slipper, displaying charm

indicators.note: in an across answer, one piece put on another is attached after it

parts.note: a mule is a backless slipper
the Model T was Ford's famous car, so Model gives T

explanation.surface: A fashion model slips on a mule and shows off her appeal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Model' looks like a person on a catwalk; it is the Model T Ford, giving just T.
explanation.definitionFit: An amulet is a charm worn to ward off evil, a lucky trinket.

clue.text: Cosmetic treatment for hyperactive waterway

parts.note: manic means frantically energetic
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire, England

explanation.surface: Beauty therapy for a restless canal.
explanation.definitionFit: A manicure is a beauty treatment for the hands and nails.

clue.text: Clear up mess left by wild party

indicators.note: a mess is a jumble, so the letters of clear up are scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone must tidy the chaos left behind by a riotous bash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mess' scrambles CLEARUP into UPERCAL, set by L.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lupercalia was a riotous ancient Roman festival; Lupercal names the feast and its grotto.

clue.text: Seem likely to be devoured after god drops round

indicators.note: in a down answer, after means this piece comes below the previous one
to drop a letter is to lose it from the word

parts.note: Thor is the Norse god of thunder
O is round in shape
eaten means devoured

explanation.surface: A deity loses a fight and seems about to be swallowed up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drops' takes O from THOR to leave THR.
explanation.definitionFit: Clouds that threaten rain seem likely to bring it, so threaten means to look probable.

clue.text: Store of Latin gathered in by outdoor worker

indicators.note: the Latin word is collected inside the store, which closes round it

parts.note: to garner is to gather and store up
de is the Latin word for 'of'

explanation.surface: A heap of Latin texts is collected by someone who works outdoors.
explanation.definitionFit: A gardener spends working days outside, tending plants and lawns.

clue.text: Onset of pain in the kidneys set back marksman

indicators.note: the first letter of pain goes inside the reversed kidneys
set back means the word for kidneys is read from the end to the start

parts.note: reins is an archaic word for the kidneys, as in the Bible

indicators.note: the onset of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A sudden twinge in the kidneys sets back a shooter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set back' turns REINS into SNIER, and 'in' places P inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A sniper is a marksman firing from a hidden position.

clue.text: Artists apply to less than saintly monk

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, so RAs are artists
to put in for something is to apply for it

explanation.surface: Painters seek a post with a monk of dubious virtue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'apply to' reads as 'put in for', giving PUT IN; 'to' just joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Grigori Rasputin was the notoriously debauched Russian holy man at the Tsar's court.

clue.text: "The slag has manners", officer admitted on reflection

indicators.note: a reflection shows a mirror image, so the whole assembly is read backwards
to be admitted is to be let inside, so the officer goes within the manners

parts.note: airs are affected manners, as in airs and graces
OC is officer commanding

explanation.surface: Someone sneers that a woman puts on airs, then an officer reconsiders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slag' reads as an insult in the surface; here it is the waste from smelting.
explanation.definitionFit: Scoria is the cinder-like waste left from smelting metal, the same as slag.

clue.text: Revolutionary BNP member from Bath concealing Tory origin?

parts.note: Bath is a famous English spa town

indicators.note: the racist hides the next letter inside

parts.note: the BNP was a far-right British party, so a member is a racist

indicators.note: a word's origin is its first letter

explanation.surface: A far-right activist from Bath hides Conservative roots and turns revolutionary.
explanation.walkthrough: The BNP (British National Party) was a far-right UK party. 'concealing' tucks T inside RACIST.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spartacists were German revolutionary socialists of 1919, so a Spartacist is a revolutionary.

clue.text: Emperor Pan devised special appellation

indicators.note: something devised is worked out anew, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A ruler named Pan invents a special title.
explanation.definitionFit: A proper noun names one particular person or place, a specific appellation rather than a common one.

clue.text: Pond-dweller's edict finds king in no condition for driving

parts.note: a bull is a papal edict

indicators.note: the king goes inside the weather that stops driving

parts.note: fog makes driving unsafe
R is short for rex, king

explanation.surface: A frog's decree finds the king unfit to drive.
explanation.definitionFit: A bullfrog is a large frog living in and around ponds.

clue.text: A decadent poet admits verse by churchman's right

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so the poet takes the verse inside

parts.note: Ernest Dowson was a poet of the 1890s Decadent movement

explanation.surface: A dissolute poet lets in verse beside a cleric's entitlement.
explanation.definitionFit: An advowson is the right to nominate a clergyman to a church living.

clue.text: Response to accusation certain to give delight

parts.note: a plea is what a defendant answers to a charge
sure means certain

explanation.surface: A defendant's reply is bound to bring joy.
explanation.definitionFit: Pleasure is a feeling of enjoyment, the same as delight.

clue.text: Waving too much, having secured a promontory

indicators.note: the excess word holds the next pieces firmly inside it

parts.note: unduly means excessively, too much
a tor is a rocky peak or outcrop

explanation.surface: Someone gestures excessively after reaching a headland.
explanation.definitionFit: Undulatory describes a rippling, wavelike motion.

clue.text: Euphemistically dead fish gobbled up by snake

indicators.note: something gobbled is swallowed whole, so the snake holds the fish inside

parts.note: an asp is a venomous snake

indicators.note: in a down answer, up means the fish word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: an eel is a fish

explanation.surface: A snake swallows a fish which is then, politely speaking, no more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses the fish in this down answer before 'gobbled' places it within the snake, giving LEE inside the snake.
explanation.definitionFit: Falling asleep, or being laid to rest, is a gentle euphemism for having died.

clue.text: A country raised to conceal name of fictional realm

indicators.note: the reversed pieces hide the abbreviation for name within
in a down answer, raised means the pieces read upwards

parts.note: Iran is a country

explanation.surface: A nation lifted to keep secret the name of an imaginary land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns A IRAN into NARIA, and 'to conceal' places N inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Narnia is the magical land of C. S. Lewis's children's novels.

clue.text: Imagine being fed to the fish!

parts.note: the ide is a freshwater fish
ate means fed, past tense of eat

explanation.surface: Picture someone being fed to the fishes!
explanation.definitionFit: To ideate is to form ideas, to picture something in the mind.

clue.text: Sponge for dessert sent back with sigh of relief

indicators.note: sent back means the dessert word is read in reverse

parts.note: a fool is a creamy fruit pudding, as in gooseberry fool
ah is an exclamation of relief

explanation.surface: A diner returns their pudding and sighs with relief, asking for a sponge cake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent back' turns FOOL into LOOF. Sponge looks like a cake beside dessert; it is the bath sponge.
explanation.definitionFit: A loofah is the dried fibrous gourd used as a bath sponge.

clue.text: Labourer covering a Test drops note of support for bowler?

indicators.note: the labourer wraps round the next pieces like a cover

parts.note: a hand is a manual worker, as in farmhand

indicators.note: to drop a letter is to let it fall out of the word

parts.note: taken as written, a cricket Test match
E is a musical note

explanation.surface: A worker shields a Test match from a dropped catch, steadying the bowler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drops' takes E from TEST to leave TST. A bowler here is a hat, not a cricketer, so a hatstand holds it up; the question mark flags this.
explanation.definitionFit: A hatstand is a pole with hooks on which hats such as bowlers are hung.

clue.text: Dodgy, squire (nudge nudge wink wink)!

indicators.note: dodgy means unsound or shady, so the word squire is shuffled

explanation.surface: A suggestive innuendo aimed at a country gentleman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nudge nudge wink wink' is the catchphrase from a Monty Python sketch signalling a smutty innuendo.
explanation.definitionFit: Risqué means slightly indecent, the kind of remark greeted with a knowing wink.

clue.text: Rupture received in the same place in Ireland

indicators.note: something received is taken in, so the rupture holds the abbreviation

parts.note: a hernia is a rupture of tissue
ib, short for ibidem, means in the same place

explanation.surface: A man suffered a hernia in the very spot in Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Hibernia is the Latin name for Ireland.

clue.text: Look at bird

definitions.meaning: a ... is a look, as in 'take a ...'

explanation.definitionFit: Gander is both the male goose and informal slang for a quick look.

clue.text: Strike second-best attendant

parts.note: top means best, as in top marks
a page is a young attendant

explanation.surface: A runner-up servant goes on strike.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoppage is a halt in work, an industrial strike.
